messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Problem with graphic interface
messages.body_plain:
Hello Sir/Madam.

My name is David Ghisi Bertoldi and am currently an undergrad business student in Brazil at Insper doing my scientific initiation on networks and performance.

I have enjoyed a lot using your program.

As that may be I have encountered a problem using the graphic interface from function siena01Gui(). I cannot add more than 20 to 25 variates. Is that common? How can I fix that?

Thank you

David Ghisi Bertoldi

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Old postings
messages.body_plain:
To all subscribers to the RSiena help list at RForge

I just cleaned up old postings to the RSiena help list at RForge. My apologies for not having done this earlier. The spam I threw away; I apologize to Maarten van Zalk that I did mistakenly accept (and thereby let through) his message that was meant for me personally.
I suggest that nobody considers the messages from 2012; I  only passed them on to let the senders know that indeed their posts were received.

Note that the RSiena help list at RForge is meant only for help with RSiena programming (i.e., the source code); for help with RSiena use (i.e., applications) please go to http://groups.yahoo.com/groups/stocnet/

Best wishes,
Tom

================================================================

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Problem with graphic interface
messages.body_plain:
Dear David,

The graphical interface siena01Gui() does not have all options that the regular use of RSiena within R has. Twenty variables is a lot; for beginning use of RSiena it is not advisable to use so many variables; for further (regular) use of RSiena, it is advisable not to use the siena01Gui() but to use the package within R as described in the manual section 2.3. R is not hard to learn!

I wish you much success,

Tom

================================================================
